key_insight: With fixed measurement and no trainable affine output processing, reachable observables expand strictly from a fixed-spectrum unitary orbit to its mixed-unitary convex hull to a CPTP operator interval for any nonconstant readout.
engineering_relevance: The hierarchy identifies when adding general quantum channels can overcome expressivity limits that deeper unitary circuits cannot remove.
method: Characterize effective Heisenberg-picture observables under unitary, mixed-unitary, and CPTP dynamics.
Use amplitude damping with a fixed Pauli readout to demonstrate separation from mixed-unitary models.
Implement CPTP dynamics through a Stinespring-channelized circuit and derive analytic loss floors.
evidence_signal: Numerics reproduce loss floors of 4γ²/3, γ², and zero for the unitary, mixed-unitary, and CPTP levels, respectively; structured-observable, Rényi-moment, and classification experiments illustrate finite-depth behavior.
watch_item: The reachable-set hierarchy does not guarantee that finite-depth channel circuits can efficiently train to the optimal observable.
paper_title: Observable-Level Expressivity in Fixed-Readout Quantum Neural Networks
